candidates.title: GPT-6.1 Sol shifts the frontier toward cost per completed task
candidates.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol as an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol, reporting materially better agentic results without increasing standard Sol token prices.
candidates.what_changed: The gpt-6.1-sol model keeps standard API pricing at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens while cutting cached input to $0.10 per million. OpenAI reports materially better coding, computer-use, professional-work, and factuality results.
candidates.why_it_matters: For long-running agents, list token price alone is an increasingly poor model-selection metric. Cache reuse, reasoning effort, task success, tool execution, retries, and total cost per accepted task can change the practical ranking between models.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Benchmark GPT-6.1 Sol against the incumbent model on complete tasks and record success, latency, reasoning effort, cached versus uncached tokens, tool calls, retries, human correction, and cost per accepted result.

evidence.rationale: Release, pricing, availability, benchmark settings, and alignment claims are documented by OpenAI. Independent reporting corroborates the release; benchmark improvements are not treated as independently reproduced.
evidence.independent_validation: Release independently reported; performance claims remain vendor-reported.
evidence.claim_scope: All benchmark, factuality, safety, and cost-per-task comparisons are OpenAI-reported unless explicitly attributed otherwise.

signal.rationale: The release materially changes the price/performance trade-off for coding, computer-use, and professional agent workloads.

deduplication.candidate_key: https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-sol/|GPT-6.1 Sol|new model price-performance and cached-input change
deduplication.material_delta: A distinct 6.1 release adds new benchmark results, halved cached-input price versus GPT-6 Sol, new API/model availability, and updated safety evaluations.

candidates.title: OpenAI Dots turn persistent background agents into a first-class product
candidates.summary: OpenAI launched Dots, persistent agents with their own cloud computers that can continue projects in the background, use connected apps, and escalate governed actions through approval and permission rules.
candidates.what_changed: A dot can maintain several ongoing projects, use a dedicated cloud computer and browser, perform read-only proactive research in connected apps, and request approval for governed actions without requiring a continuously open user session.
candidates.why_it_matters: Persistent delegated work makes permissions, background monitoring, state continuity, interruption, and review surfaces core engineering concerns rather than optional UX details.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Inspect default permissions, background-action limits, credential isolation, approval rules, audit visibility, pause/stop behavior, and how persistent state is scoped across projects.

evidence.rationale: OpenAI documents product behavior, availability, permission model, cloud-computer boundary, and proactive-research restrictions; Reuters independently corroborates the launch and broad product model.
evidence.independent_validation: Launch corroborated by Reuters; safeguard effectiveness and long-horizon reliability were not independently reproduced in this run.
evidence.claim_scope: Treat safeguard effectiveness and autonomous reliability as OpenAI-reported design claims, not independently proven guarantees.

signal.rationale: Persistent background agents change the operational and permission model engineers must reason about when delegating multi-step work.

deduplication.material_delta: New persistent-agent product and control model.

candidates.title: Holo4 packages GUI, code, MCP, and API actions into one open-weight agent model
candidates.summary: H Company released Holo4, a family of computer-use vision-language models designed to act through GUIs, code, MCP, and APIs, with downloadable weights and evaluation trajectories.
candidates.what_changed: The release includes a 27B dense model under CC BY-NC 4.0 and a 35B-A3B mixture-of-experts variant described as Apache 2.0, plus an agent harness, trajectories, and vendor benchmark results.
candidates.why_it_matters: Open-weight computer-use models are moving toward a unified action policy that can choose between visual interaction, code execution, and structured tools.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Evaluate model and harness together, including held-out task success, trajectory quality, recovery, latency, hardware footprint, and license constraints; cross-vendor OSWorld scores are not directly interchangeable across harnesses and settings.

evidence.rationale: Weights, model cards, licenses, harness behavior, and trajectories are publicly inspectable. Benchmark scores and cost comparisons remain primarily H Company-reported.
evidence.independent_validation: Release and license details are externally inspectable; no independent benchmark reproduction was established in this run.
evidence.claim_scope: Cross-vendor benchmark comparisons are directional because harnesses, subsets, and effort settings differ.

signal.rationale: A commercially self-hostable variant combines computer use, code, MCP, and API actions in one open-weight agent model family.

deduplication.candidate_key: https://huggingface.co/blog/Hcompany/holo4|Holo4|open-weight unified GUI code MCP API agent model
deduplication.material_delta: New open-weight Holo4 family, harness, trajectories, and hybrid action interfaces.

watchlist.title: OpenAI reportedly delays GPT-6.1 Astra after safety concerns
watchlist.summary: Multiple major outlets report that OpenAI delayed or shelved a planned GPT-6.1 Astra release after internal safety concerns, but this run still did not locate a canonical OpenAI disclosure or technical evaluation supporting the reported details.

evidence.rationale: Independent reporting is substantial, but the primary technical evidence required by the current decision engine remains unavailable.

signal.rationale: A frontier-model release stopped on agentic safety grounds would materially affect model governance and deployment practice if confirmed.

promote_when: OpenAI publishes a canonical disclosure of the release decision
the underlying safety evaluation or system-card evidence becomes available

watchlist.title: MongoDB launches Atlas Agent Engine as a public-preview agent control plane
watchlist.summary: MongoDB announced Atlas Agent Engine as a public-preview execution, memory, retrieval, and governance layer while its preview policy says preview features are for evaluation and are not production-ready or covered by standard support and SLAs.

evidence.rationale: The launch and feature claims are first-party, while MongoDB's own preview policy creates a deployment caveat that makes production-readiness framing premature.

signal.rationale: The architecture is relevant, but current public-preview status limits what engineers should infer about production readiness today.

promote_when: Agent Engine receives production-ready or generally available status
product-specific documentation clarifies runtime, governance, support, and failure semantics sufficiently for a precise engineering assessment
